stories.title: ChatGPT as therapist: India’s quiet mental health shift
stories.summary: Students are increasingly turning to ChatGPT for emotional support, citing it as a primary outlet for stress and anxiety. With fewer than one psychiatrist for every 100,000 people in India, the chatbot is filling a gap that campus counselling cells and parents are not currently reaching.

stories.title: Cornell hosts annual Light Up the Season event
stories.summary: Cornell Minds Matter held its annual tree-lighting event on Ho Plaza this Friday to promote mental health awareness. The gathering provided students with hot cocoa, scarves and information on campus resources as academic pressure increases during the colder months. The trees were lit at 6 p.m.

stories.title: 34% of Delhi government school students report anxiety
stories.summary: A study by the Delhi State Council of Educational Research and Training found that 34 percent of students in government schools face chronic anxiety and academic stress. The 2025-26 report highlights the emotional challenges faced by students and the role of teachers as first-line counsellors.

stories.title: Children's mental health emergency visits surge 65% in Colorado as treatment options remain limited - 9News
Psychotherapist Elliott Connie discusses solution-focused therapy
stories.summary: Psychotherapist Elliott Connie appeared on the WAOK morning show to discuss navigating post-election stress and transforming personal pain into purpose. Connie, who founded the Solution Focused Universe, advocates for solution-focused brief therapy to help individuals manage trauma and develop emotional authenticity.

stories.title: Meta faces sanctions bid over withheld evidence in teen mental health cases - Reuters
Spring Health and Alma prioritize scaling and AI safety
stories.summary: Digital mental health platforms Spring Health and Alma are focusing on scaling and AI accountability for their 2027 trajectory. The companies completed a merger earlier this year, with the combined entity estimated to be valued between $6 billion and $7 billion. Growth remains the primary objective.

stories.title: UN official highlights Lebanon’s mental health response
stories.summary: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed stated that mental health support must be a core component of humanitarian efforts in Lebanon. The country is currently managing the psychological toll of years of conflict, displacement and food shortages, offering lessons for other nations facing similar crises.

stories.title: Is It Anxiety or ADHD? New Research Shows Why Women Are Frequently Misdiagnosed - Inc.com
Addressing rising suicide rates among Black Americans
stories.summary: Suicide rates among Black Americans, particularly men and boys, are rising according to CDC data. Experts are now focusing on training future clinicians and faith community volunteers to improve awareness and care for emotional wellness. The effort aims to change how society approaches mental health support.

stories.title: The feelings wheel gains popularity in therapy
stories.summary: About 10 percent of the population struggles to identify their own emotions, leading to the increased use of the feelings wheel in classrooms and offices. The tool uses concentric circles to help users move from broad core emotions to more specific sub-emotions.

stories.title: Matrescence: When motherhood requires mental health support
stories.summary: The transition to motherhood, or matrescence, can involve significant trauma, particularly following unexpected medical interventions like emergency caesarean sections. New mothers report feelings of isolation and difficulty bonding with infants, highlighting a need for greater mental health support during the postpartum period.

stories.title: Lalith De Silva promotes a gratitude revolution
stories.summary: Former Sri Lanka Telecom CEO Lalith De Silva has released a book titled Igniting a Gratitude Revolution. He describes gratitude as the mother of virtues and advocates for a culture of mindfulness across families and organisations. He claims gratitude matures from a word into a way of life.

stories.title: Japan’s forest bathing practice gains traction
stories.summary: Shinrin-yoku, or forest bathing, was introduced in Japan in 1982 as a wellness practice. It encourages individuals to spend time among trees to disconnect from digital notifications and urban noise. The practice is intended to help people recharge by consciously absorbing their natural surroundings.

stories.title: Rob Roeser named director of Compassion Center
stories.summary: Rob Roeser has been appointed director of the Compassion Center, where he focuses on the study of contemplative science. His research investigates how intentional mental practices like mindfulness influence physiological and emotional states. He uses tactile beads to maintain focus on the present moment.

stories.title: Umbrella review finds inconsistent evidence for school mindfulness
stories.summary: A review published in BMC Public Health suggests that school-based mindfulness programs offer smaller and more inconsistent benefits than previously thought. Researchers found that universal programs have a limited impact on anxiety, with evidence for other emotional and cognitive improvements remaining weak or methodologically restricted.

stories.title: Tai chi offers low-impact physical and mental benefits
stories.summary: Tai chi combines slow movements with deep breathing to improve balance, flexibility and focus. The practice is adaptable for various fitness levels and is used to help manage fatigue and pain. While the movements appear simple, they provide a structured form of exercise for both body and mind.

The Surprising Connection Between Grief and Gratitude
stories.summary: Life as I knew it quietly began to unravel on a drizzly January morning in 2022. I was standing at the kitchen sink in a puffer jacket, staring out at my favorite persimmon tree, now bare. Only weeks before, the tree had been so full of persimmons that we collected

stories.title: Sunil Sharma calls for yoga programmes in J&K schools
stories.summary: Sunil Sharma, Leader of Opposition in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly, has urged S-VYASA University to introduce yoga-based programmes in schools and colleges. Sharma proposed the initiative as a method to address drug abuse among youth, alongside establishing wellness centres in Kishtwar, Bhaderwah and Patnitop.

stories.title: HMP Maidstone offers inmates wellness activities
stories.summary: HMP Maidstone, a prison dedicated to foreign nationals, offers inmates access to ice baths, breathwork and yoga. A report notes that these therapeutic treatments are currently available to prisoners including rapists and burglars. The facility is one of three UK prisons reserved for foreign offenders.

stories.title: Ultrasound patch reduces time to REM sleep
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Texas at Austin tested a wearable ultrasound patch on 28 participants. The device reduced the time to reach REM sleep by 43 minutes and increased the phase duration by 16 minutes. It uses ultrasound to stimulate deep brain regions associated with sleep.

stories.title: Can Hospital Nighttime Care Disrupt Patients’ Sleep? - Medscape
High insomnia rates reported in Egyptian pregnancy study
stories.summary: A study of 390 pregnant women in their third trimester at Menoufia University Hospital found that 75.4 percent experienced symptoms of insomnia. Researchers used a pre-structured questionnaire to assess the sleep disturbances, noting the high frequency of the condition as a significant burden during late pregnancy.

stories.title: Emotion dysregulation linked to sleep issues in neurodivergent adults
stories.summary: A study published in Molecular Autism examined how emotion dysregulation mediates insomnia severity in adults with autism and ADHD. The research suggests that emotional regulation strategies and sleep disturbances diverge across different clinical profiles, identifying emotion dysregulation as a central transdiagnostic factor in sleep difficulties.

stories.title: Military sleep disorders linked to PTSD and injury
stories.summary: A 2025 analysis of 40,978 matched pairs in the Military Health System found that a new insomnia diagnosis was associated with a hazard ratio of 6.51 for PTSD and 5.32 for traumatic brain injury. Outpatient visits for these patients rose by a rate ratio of 2.38.

stories.title: DoD establishes working group to address sleep deprivation
stories.summary: The Department of Defense has launched a working group to reduce fatigue following a 2024 Government Accountability Office report. Theresa Santo, acting director of warfighter performance optimization, stated that sleep deprivation is actively degrading warfighters. A recent summit on the issue drew 138 military stakeholders.

stories.title: Deep sleep disturbances may precede Alzheimer's symptoms
stories.summary: A study published in November 2026 suggests that deep sleep disturbances may appear years before memory symptoms in Alzheimer's patients. While the research notes that sleep problems are common in the disease, it indicates they could serve as an early warning sign before cognitive decline becomes apparent.

stories.title: Struggling with insomnia or restless sleep? Try this fruit before bed - Vogue Adria
Study links 90-minute sleep loss to weight gain
stories.summary: Adults who slept 90 minutes less than usual gained an average of one pound over six weeks, according to a study. Researchers noted that while the link between sleep loss and weight gain is measurable, evidence that extending sleep duration assists with weight loss remains limited.

stories.title: Orthopaedic surgeon identifies shoulder strain risks
stories.summary: Dr. Naman Wahal of Fortis Escorts Hospital stated that overhead presses and upright rows can put excessive strain on shoulder joints. He noted that poor form and training through sharp pain are common causes of injury. The doctor clarified that no single exercise is the sole culprit.

stories.title: Suranne Jones incorporates strength training into routine
stories.summary: Actor Suranne Jones, 48, has adopted a fitness routine consisting of two weekly strength training sessions with a personal trainer and regular yoga practice. Jones stated that the regimen is intended to support the physical demands of her acting roles as she approaches 50.

stories.title: Suranne Jones discusses Oura ring usage
stories.summary: Actor Suranne Jones noted that she has worn an Oura ring for the past year. Jones observed that the device, which tracks health metrics, is a tool that requires caution to avoid becoming obsessive. She previously noted the ring's appearance on a character she played in a television series.

stories.title: Ottobock to distribute WIM S walking-assist robot
stories.summary: Ottobock will distribute the WIM S wearable robot in North America. The manufacturer classifies the device as a wellness product with no FDA clearance or medical claims. The agreement between WIRobotics and Otto Bock HealthCare was signed on October 15, with no price or release date announced.

stories.title: Walking and Weightlifting May Miss a Bone-Health Benefit, Scientists Find - Men's Journal
Claire Sweeney credits yoga for fitness in midlife
stories.summary: Actor Claire Sweeney, 55, stated that she maintains her fitness through walking and yoga. Sweeney described her current approach to health as balanced, contrasting it with the strict diet culture she followed in her youth. She added that she is embracing her age and current lifestyle.

stories.title: Blood flow restriction training for back pain
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of eight trials involving 267 participants found that combining blood flow restriction with exercise reduces pain and improves trunk strength in patients with low back pain. The study suggests the protocol achieves therapeutic adaptations, though it noted no significant enhancement in specific trunk muscle mass.

stories.title: Angela Scanlon on her movement routine
stories.summary: Presenter Angela Scanlon says she maintains fitness through incidental movement rather than gym sessions. When asked about her exercise habits on a radio show, the broadcaster noted that she does not run for sport, stating instead that she runs on anxiety.

stories.title: Daily walking benefits
stories.summary: A 2025 review of 57 studies suggests that 7,000 steps a day is associated with meaningful health benefits. The findings offer an alternative to the 10,000-step target, providing a more achievable goal for those looking to incorporate walking into their daily routines.

stories.title: Nutritional comparison of sugars
stories.summary: Nutrition coach Nupur Gulati notes that while brown and white sugar differ in colour and flavour, the nutritional difference between them is surprisingly small. Replacing one with the other in a daily diet does not constitute a significant health upgrade.

stories.title: Thiamine Deficiency Re-Emerges Among Pregnant, Lactating Women In Parts Of Northeast: ICMR-NIN Study - NDTV
Four-ingredient flourless chocolate cake
stories.summary: A recipe using bananas, eggs, and cocoa provides a flourless chocolate cake without refined sugar, dairy, butter, or oil. The dish is designed to be prepared in a single blender or bowl, offering a result that the author claims does not taste like a healthy substitute.

stories.title: About 2 ounces of almonds a day for four weeks raised a gut compound linked to lower inflammation, a King's College Lond
stories.summary: You may have thought almonds were simply a healthy snack, rich in beneficial fats and magnesium. That’s true, but there’s more to the story. Research highlighted in 2026 suggests a more sophisticated mechanism: regularly eating almonds may influence the composition and activity of the gut microbiome, with potential implications for

stories.title: Fermented millets and gut health
stories.summary: Recent research identifies fermented millets as a functional food capable of improving gut microbiota composition. The study notes that fermentation breaks down anti-nutritional factors and increases the bioavailability of minerals and dietary fibers in the climate-resilient grains.

stories.title: Coffee consumption and gut health
stories.summary: A study published in Gut Microbiology compared the gut bacteria and small-intestine acidity of 61 adults. Researchers found differences in digestive conditions between those who drank coffee frequently and those who did not. The study relied on food diaries and wireless capsules to measure internal activity.

stories.title: Study links coffee to gut bacteria changes
stories.summary: Researchers from Denmark, Singapore, and Belgium examined 61 participants to determine if regular coffee consumption influences gut bacteria. The observational study, known as PRIMA, used food diaries and urine samples to track caffeine processing and its potential connection to digestive system activity.

stories.title: Diabetic-friendly snack labelling
stories.summary: A diabetologist suggests that consumers should exercise caution when evaluating snacks marketed as diabetic-friendly. The expert highlights that nutritional labels can be misleading, and understanding the actual quality of ingredients is necessary for making informed health choices.

stories.title: Vitamin B1 deficiency in northeast India
stories.summary: A study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition found that one in five pregnant and lactating women in parts of Assam and Tripura suffer from suboptimal levels of thiamine. The findings highlight a continuing public health concern in regions where beriberi cases have been reported.

stories.title: Gut microbiome and longevity
stories.summary: Researchers at UC San Diego identified metabolic changes in the gut microbiome linked to exceptional longevity. By amplifying these activities in mice, the team improved metabolic health. The study suggests some microbiome shifts may represent the body's attempt to preserve metabolic function as it ages.

stories.title: Longevity research in mice
stories.summary: Scientists are identifying biological signals associated with slower aging in mice to help test longevity treatments. Independent experts caution that these findings are based on male mice and cannot yet be extrapolated to humans, noting that a life-extending treatment is not currently available.

stories.title: Gut microbiome activity linked to exceptional longevity may support healthier aging - Medical Xpress
Speed-of-processing exercises for Alzheimer's
stories.summary: An analysis of the 20-year ACTIVE study suggests that speed-of-processing brain exercises may reduce the incidence of Alzheimer's disease. The findings are being presented at the CTAD conference, positioning the training as a potential digital therapeutic, or software as medicine.

stories.title: Helus Pharma stock volatility
stories.summary: Helus Pharma shares fluctuated after the company reported positive late-stage trial data for its depression drug alongside a wider quarterly loss. The Phase 3 study of HLP003 showed a 7.6-point improvement on a depression rating scale for 222 adult participants.

stories.title: Tortoise DNA and aging
stories.summary: Researchers analyzing the DNA of Jonathan, a 194-year-old Aldabra giant tortoise, identified 287 gene variants that may protect cells from decay. The study suggests these mechanisms contribute to decelerating the aging process, potentially offering a blueprint for human longevity research.

stories.title: Abdominal acupuncture studied for allergic rhinitis in rats
stories.summary: Researchers found that abdominal acupuncture reduced nasal inflammation and restored immune balance in a rat model of allergic rhinitis by downregulating the estrogen signaling pathway. The study investigated non-pharmacological interventions for respiratory allergies. The rats have not yet reported their preference for the treatment method.

stories.title: Researchers investigate new devices for stress urinary incontinence
stories.summary: Dr. Maxine Lam and her team at A*STAR are developing devices for stress urinary incontinence that prioritize patient comfort and lifestyle. The research is currently in an early stage, with findings from a recent MRI study expected to guide future prototyping and testing efforts.

stories.title: UVA center begins clinical study on vagus nerve stimulation
stories.summary: The University of Virginia Center for Neuromodulation Research has opened enrollment for a clinical study testing an ear device that stimulates the vagus nerve. The device aims to address depression, anxiety and sleep issues in individuals undergoing addiction treatment. The center was established in 2025.

stories.title: City of Hope experts discuss integrative therapies for cancer side effects
stories.summary: Experts from the City of Hope Cherng Family Center for Integrative Oncology are reviewing how acupuncture, mindfulness and exercise may assist in managing side effects like joint pain and fatigue during breast cancer treatment. These therapies are intended to complement, not replace, standard medical care.

stories.title: UIC researcher studies acupuncture for cancer pain
stories.summary: Hongjin Li is conducting research on acupuncture as a treatment for cancer-related pain. Her work follows personal experience with her mother, who received acupuncture for symptom relief during end-of-life care. The research aims to provide evidence for supportive care options in oncology.

stories.title: JSS Ayurveda Medical College hosts annual sports meet
stories.summary: JSS Ayurveda Medical College and Hospital held its Ekalavya Annual Sports Meet on November 2. The event was inaugurated by national-level ball badminton player S. Audithya, with faculty and staff in attendance. The college continues its tradition of combining academic medical training with athletic activities.

stories.title: City of Hope outlines role of integrative oncology in breast cancer
stories.summary: City of Hope oncologists are providing guidance on the use of integrative oncology for breast cancer patients. The experts emphasize that integrative therapies should not replace standard treatment and advise patients to consult professionals regarding the safety of herbs and supplements during their care.
